focus: Angle 11 — version authority across routing artifacts

findingDetails.title: system-deep-loop description.json advertises the previous release against SKILL.md and both sibling hubs
findingDetails.evidence: description.json:4 = 2.2.3.0, exactly changelog/v2.2.3.0.md, while SKILL.md:3 = 3.0.0.0 = changelog/v3.0.0.0.md. sk-code/SKILL.md:5 = description.json:4 = 4.2.2.0 = newest changelog; cli-external-orchestration/SKILL.md:5 = description.json:4 = 1.5.0.0 = newest changelog. 17 of 17 mode-packet SKILL.md files equal their newest changelog entry, establishing the release rule the hub identity pair breaks.
findingDetails.impact: The advisor-facing identity file a reader meets first states a version one release behind the skill it describes, in the one hub of three that fails to keep the pair.
findingDetails.recommendation: Set description.json version to 3.0.0.0 (or regenerate it from the release) and add a gate comparing SKILL.md against the newest changelog. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Read every version field at its line, listed every changelog entry under all three hub roots and all seventeen mode roots, and verified no generator or gate stamps or compares description.json (regenerate-skill-derived.cjs preserves authored fields; ci-skill-root-metadata never writes authored files).

findingDetails.title: Registry/router version fields match neither their hub release nor each other in 2 of 3 hubs, and sk-code's paired value lags its release
findingDetails.evidence: system-deep-loop registry 2.0.0.1 vs router 2.0.1.1 vs release 3.0.0.0; cli-external-orchestration registry 1.2.0.2 vs router 1.2.1.2 vs release 1.5.0.0; sk-code registry == router == 4.1.0.1 while its changelog has shipped v4.2.0.0, v4.2.1.0 and v4.2.2.0. ROUTER.md drifts in all three hubs (1.0.1.0 / 3.5.0.9 / 1.1.0.0). parent-skills-nested-packets.md:105 calls the registry field a four-part version for hubs that ship releases; no observed value equals its release.
findingDetails.impact: A reader cannot tell whether the registry/router version names the hub release, a schema generation, or nothing at all, and no release bumps them.
findingDetails.recommendation: Decide the field's meaning once: either synchronize it to the release or rename it (registrySchemaVersion/routerSchemaVersion) with a documented value and a validator. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Verified each hub value at its exact line, re-ran wave one's F009 pairing check hub by hub, read both authoring docs that define the field, and searched every compiler/gate/runtime module for a version consumer (none reads it).

findingDetails.title: hub-router schema doc defines version as either router schema or artifact version in one sentence, and nothing validates it
findingDetails.evidence: parent-hub-router-schema.md:53 reads 'Router schema or artifact version for the hub'; the field can legitimately mean schema generation or release, and the observed fleet splits along the ambiguity. ci-skill-root-metadata.cjs:40 states the seven authored files are reported and never regenerated; :191-229 byte-compares only the manifest; required-file contract skill-root-metadata-contract.cjs:74 lists presence, not version values. No compiler, gate or runtime module reads any artifact version field.
findingDetails.impact: The ambiguity is the root mechanism that keeps F021 and F022 permanently unresolvable by reading; each authoring pass inherits it.
findingDetails.recommendation: Split the doc's cell into the two possible meanings and name which one the file carries; pair it with the F022 decision. No fix was made during this review.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Read the schema doc table cell directly, then confirmed the absence of any validator by reading the fleet gate's manifest-only byte comparison and its contract's required-file list, and by grepping the compilers for version consumers.

reviewDepthApplicability.reason: Twenty version-bearing artifacts across three hubs, seventeen mode packets, three changelog histories and two authoring-doc authorities, with every value read at its exact line and every consumer searched.

targetSelection.selectionReason: Angle 11 names version authority and every disagreement across three hubs and their modes; the changelogs are the only artifact family that must move on every release, and the authoring docs are the only in-tree field authorities.

searchLedger.hypothesis: The advisor identity file tracks the hub release that SKILL.md announces.

searchActions.queryOrPath: description.json version against every changelog entry and both sibling hubs
searchActions.result: 2.2.3.0 is the changelog two entries back; SKILL.md and both sibling identity files equal their newest changelog entry.

searchLedger.rationale: Two hubs pair the identity file with the release; one lags exactly one release behind.

searchLedger.invariant: A version field that names the hub release must equal the hub release, or say what else it names.

searchActions.queryOrPath: registry/router/ROUTER.md versions for all three hubs against newest changelogs
searchActions.result: All nine values differ from their releases; two hubs split their registry/router pair, the third pairs at a lagging value.

searchLedger.rationale: Documented meaning contradicts observed values fleet-wide.

searchLedger.hypothesis: The authoring doc resolves what the router version names.

searchActions.queryOrPath: parent-hub-router-schema.md version row and parent-skills-nested-packets.md registry field list
searchActions.result: One doc says 'Router schema or artifact version', the other says 'four-part version for hubs that ship releases'; neither resolves.

searchLedger.rationale: The ambiguity is the mechanism that permits every disagreement found above.

searchLedger.invariant: Every mode packet's SKILL.md equals the newest changelog under its own root.

searchActions.queryOrPath: 17 mode-packet SKILL.md versions against their changelog listings
searchActions.result: 17/17 equal, making the mode layer the positive control for the release rule.

searchLedger.rationale: The mode layer obeys the authority rule exactly; the drift is confined to hub-root artifact families.

searchLedger.hypothesis: Some gate compares hub-root version fields and would catch the drift.

searchActions.queryOrPath: every compiler, gate and runtime module for reads of registry.version/hubRouter.version/description.version
searchActions.result: No consumer; compilers read resourceContractVersion, the fleet gate byte-compares only leaf-manifest.json and never rewrites the seven authored files.

searchLedger.rationale: The absence is itself evidence folded into F023 rather than a separate finding: the goal was to test whether F021/F022 are machine-caught, and they are not.
searchLedger.ruledOutReason: No version comparator exists anywhere in the fleet gates.
